function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common ways to get a cake delivered (or pick it up) in the U.S. – and a few tips to help you choose the right option for your needs. | What you’re looking for | Best option | How to find it | Tips | |--------------------------|-------------|----------------|------| | **Custom, high‑end cakes** | Local artisan bakeries (e.g., Magnolia Bakery, Baked by Melissa, or a boutique bakery in your city) | • Google “custom cake bakery near me”
• Yelp or TripAdvisor reviews
• Instagram hashtags like #customcakes | • Order at least 1–2 weeks in advance for big orders.
• Ask for a tasting or sample if you’re ordering a large cake. | | **Same‑day delivery** | Online cake‑delivery platforms (Goldbelly, Cake Delivery, or local delivery services) | • Visit Goldbelly.com and search “cake”
• Use the “Delivery” filter on local grocery sites (Walmart, Kroger, Publix) | • Check delivery windows; many sites offer “same‑day” or “next‑day” options.
• Verify the cake’s temperature requirements (some need refrigeration). | | **Convenience & price** | Grocery‑store bakeries (Walmart, Kroger, Publix, Safeway) | • Check the store’s website or app for “Bakery”
• Look for “Online Order & Pickup” or “Delivery” | • Many grocery stores now offer curb‑side pickup or delivery via Instacart.
• Prices are usually lower than specialty bakeries. | | **Specialty flavors (e.g., vegan, gluten‑free)** | Specialty bakeries or health‑food stores | • Search “vegan cake delivery” or “gluten‑free cake”
• Look at local health‑food co‑ops or organic markets | • Confirm ingredient lists; some “vegan” cakes still contain dairy‑derived ingredients. | | **Party‑size cakes (8‑12 inches)** | Party‑food delivery services (e.g., Party City, Costco, Sam’s Club) | • Costco’s “Bakery” section (online or in‑store)
• Party City’s “Cake” section | • Costco often offers large cakes at a great price; they’re usually pre‑made. | | **Last‑minute orders** | Same‑day delivery apps (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Postmates) | • Open the app, search “cake” or “bakery”
• Filter by “delivery” | • Availability depends on local restaurants or bakeries that partner with the app. | | **International or niche cakes** | Specialty import bakeries or niche online shops | • Search “imported cake delivery”
• Look for niche sites like “The Cake Shop” or “Cakes & Bakes” | • Shipping times can be longer; check shipping policies. | ### Quick‑Start Checklist 1. **Know the occasion** – Birthday, wedding, corporate event, etc. 2. **Set a budget** – Artisan cakes can cost $50–$200+; grocery‑store cakes are $20–$50. 3. **Decide on delivery vs. pickup** – Delivery saves time but may add a fee. 4. **Check the deadline** – Most bakeries require 1–2 weeks’ notice for custom orders. 5. **Read reviews** – Look for photos, taste ratings, and delivery reliability. 6. **Confirm the cake’s size & shape** – Make sure it fits your venue or plate. 7. **Ask about dietary restrictions** – Gluten‑free, nut‑free, vegan, etc. ### Example Search Paths - **Google**: “custom chocolate cake delivery in [Your City]” - **Yelp**: “best cake bakery” + “delivery” + “[Your ZIP]” - **Goldbelly**: Browse “Cake” category → filter by “Delivery” → choose a bakery that ships to your state. - **Instacart**: Search “cake” → select a local grocery store → add to cart → schedule delivery. ### Final Thought If you’re in a major metro area, you’ll likely find a mix of local artisan bakeries, national chains, and online delivery services all competing for your cake order. For the best experience, start with a clear idea of what you want (flavor, size, dietary needs) and then use the tools above to compare options. Happy cake hunting!
